Description: explicit — validate style JSON with CLI tool after migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and want to check whether my exported style JSON is compatible before deploying. Is there a CLI tool I can run on the file?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
### Yes – MapLibre ships a **style-spec validator** you can run from the command line. The tool lives in the **`@maplibre/maplibre-style-spec`** package (the same repo that defines the MapLibre style spec). Running it against your exported JSON will tell you whether the file conforms to the **MapLibre GL JS** style schema and will point out any Mapbox-only constructs that need to be changed. --- ## 1. Install / run the validator (one-off) ```bash # No permanent install needed – just invoke it with npx npx gl-style-validate path/to/your-style.json ``` *If you prefer a local dev dependency:* ```bash npm i -D @maplibre/maplibre-style-spec # then npx gl-style-validate path/to/your-style.json ``` The command prints **human-readable diagnostics** and exits with a non-zero status code if the style is invalid. --- ## 2. What the validator checks | Category | What it looks for | Typical Mapbox-only issues it will flag | |----------|-------------------|----------------------------------------| | **Top-level keys** | `version`, `sources`, `layers`, `sprite`, `glyphs`, `metadata`, `sky` (MapLibre) | Presence of `fog` (Mapbox v2) – use `sky` instead | | **Source definitions** | `type`, `url`, `tiles`, `minzoom`, `maxzoom`, `scheme`, `attribution` | `type: "vector"` with a `url: "mapbox://…"` – replace with a public/your own tile URL | | **Layer definitions** | `id`, `type`, `source`, `source-layer`, `layout`, `paint` | `source-layer` names that belong to Mapbox’s tile schema (e.g., `road`, `building`) – must match the new source | | **Sprite & glyph URLs** | Must be absolute HTTP(S) URLs or relative paths | `sprite: "mapbox://sprites/…"` or `glyphs: "mapbox://fonts/…"` – replace with URLs that serve PNG/JSON sprites or PBF glyphs | | **Expressions & layout/paint properties** | Conformance to the MapLibre style spec (v8) | Use of Mapbox-only properties (e.g., `fill-extrusion-pattern` with a Mapbox sprite name) | | **Version** | Must be `8` (the current spec version) | Older version numbers (`7`, `6`) – upgrade the JSON (the validator will suggest missing required fields) | If the validator finds a problem, it prints a line like: ``` ERROR sources.my-source.url: "mapbox://…" is not a valid URL for MapLibre ERROR layers[12].source-layer: "road" does not exist in source "my-source" WARN root.fog: property is not allowed – use "sky" instead ``` You can then edit the JSON (or the source you exported from Mapbox Studio) to replace those values. --- ## 3. Quick “fix-it” checklist after the validator runs 1. **Remove every `mapbox://` URL** * `style`, `sprite`, `glyphs`, and any source `url`. * Replace with a public style (e.g., `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty`) or with your own hosted tiles, sprites, and glyphs. 2. **Swap `fog` → `sky`** * If you need atmospheric effects, add a `sky` object (see the MapLibre spec for the allowed fields). * Example: ```json "sky": { "sky-type": "atmosphere", "sky-color": "#199EF3", "horizon-color": "#ffffff", "fog-color": "#0000ff", "fog-ground-blend": 0.5 } ``` 3. **Validate source-layer names** * Open the vector tile source you plan to use (e.g., an OSM-based source) and confirm the layer names (`road`, `building`, `water`, …). * Update any `source-layer` values that still reference Mapbox’s schema. 4. **Check sprite & glyph hosting** * Host a sprite sheet (`sprite.png` + `sprite.json`) and glyph PBFs, or point to a provider that does (e.g., MapTiler, OpenMapTiles). * Update the `sprite` and `glyphs` fields accordingly. 5. **Run the validator again** until it reports **0 errors** (warnings are okay but worth reviewing). --- ## 4. Visual sanity-check (optional but helpful) - **Maputnik** – a web UI for editing and previewing MapLibre styles. ```bash npx maputnik # then open http://localhost:8080 and load your JSON ``` It will instantly highlight missing sprites, glyphs, or source-layer mismatches. - **MapLibre GL JS quick test** – spin up a tiny HTML page that loads the style: ```html
``` If the map renders without console errors, you’re good to go. --- ## 5. TL;DR – One-liner for CI / pre-deploy Add a script to your `package.json`: ```json { "scripts": { "validate:style": "gl-style-validate ./src/style.json" } } ``` Then run (or put in CI): ```bash npm run validate:style # exits 0 on success, >0 on failure ``` If the command passes, your style JSON is **compatible with MapLibre GL JS** and ready for deployment. --- ### References | Resource | What you’ll find | |----------|------------------| | **CLI tool** | `npx gl-style-validate` – official validator (see ) | | **Style spec** | Full MapLibre style schema –  | | **Maputnik** | Interactive editor –  | | **Example OpenFreeMap style** | `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` (works out-of-the-box with MapLibre) | Give the validator a run; if it reports no errors you can safely ship the style with your migrated MapLibre map. Happy mapping!

Description: implicit — tile source with no API key needed during migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox to MapLibre and removed my access token, but now my mapbox:// style won't load. How can I test my map against a tile service that doesn't require an API key?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a **quick-start checklist** you can follow right now to get a working MapLibre map that does **not** need any API key. It shows a complete, minimal example, explains why the `mapbox://…` style fails, and gives you a handful of ready-made, free-of-charge tile services you can point to while you work on your own style. --- ## 1️⃣ Why the `mapbox://` style breaks | What you had | Why it fails after removing the token | |--------------|--------------------------------------| | `style: 'mapbox://styles/your-account/streets-v12'` | The URL is a **Mapbox-only protocol** (`mapbox://`). It tells the client to fetch the style JSON **and every source, sprite, glyph, and tile** from Mapbox’s CDN, which requires a valid `mapboxgl.accessToken`. Without a token the request is rejected (401) and the map stays blank. | | `mapboxgl.accessToken = 'pk.…'` | You removed this line, so even if the token were still present the client would never send it. | **Result:** MapLibre can’t load the style at all, because it never knows where to get the vector tiles, sprites, or fonts. --- ## 2️⃣ The easiest “drop-in” test style (no key required) ### OpenFreeMap – a complete vector style hosted by a community project ```js // 👉 Replace ONLY the `style` property (everything else can stay the same) const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', // id of the
style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', // <-- free, no token center: [-122.42, 37.78], // lon, lat zoom: 12 }); ``` *Why this works* * The URL is a **plain HTTPS URL** (not `mapbox://`). * The style JSON it returns already contains **vector source URLs**, **sprite**, and **glyph** URLs that are publicly accessible (no token, CORS already allowed). * The style is built on OpenStreetMap data, so you get a familiar “streets” look out of the box. > **Tip:** If you open the URL in a browser you’ll see the raw style JSON. You can copy it, edit it locally, or load it into **Maputnik** (the open-source style editor) to start customizing. --- ## 3️⃣ Other ready-made, key-free style URLs you can try | Service | Example style URL | What you get | Notes | |---------|-------------------|--------------|-------| | **MapLibre demo style** (the one used in the official docs) | `https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json` | Simple light basemap with OSM vector tiles | Great for a “bare-bones” test. | | **OpenStreetMap raster tiles** (via a simple raster style) | `https://{s}.tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` (use a raster-only style) | Classic OSM raster tiles | No vector data, but works everywhere. | | **Stamen Terrain** (raster) | `https://stamen-tiles.a.ssl.fastly.net/terrain/{z}/{x}/{y}.png` | Terrain raster basemap | Good for quick visual checks. | | **MapTiler Free style** (requires a token **only** for the “Free” tier; you can use the public demo token) | `https://api.maptiler.com/maps/streets/style.json?key=YOUR_KEY` | Modern vector style | If you want a MapTiler style, sign up for a free key (no credit-card needed). | | **OpenMapTiles** (self-hosted or public demo) | `https://free.tilehosting.com/data/v3.json?key=YOUR_KEY` | Full OSM vector tiles | Public demo key is rate-limited; best for prototyping. | > **Quick test:** just replace the `style` line in your map constructor with any of the URLs above and reload the page. If the map appears, you’ve confirmed that the rest of your code (markers, controls, event listeners, etc.) works with MapLibre. --- ## 4️⃣ Full minimal example (HTML + JS) ```html MapLibre test – no API key
``` *Save this as `index.html` and open it in a modern browser (Chrome ≥ 92, Firefox ≥ 90, Edge ≥ 92). The map should load instantly, no token required.* --- ## 5️⃣ If you need **your own custom style** 1. **Export the Mapbox style JSON** (if you already have one in Mapbox Studio). *File → Export → Download style JSON*. 2. **Open the JSON in Maputnik** (https://maputnik.github.io/). *File → Open → paste the JSON*. 3. **Replace every `source` URL that starts with `mapbox://`** *Typical patterns*: ```json "source": { "type": "vector", "url": "mapbox://mapbox.mapbox-streets-v8" } ``` → Change to a public vector source, e.g. an OpenMapTiles endpoint: ```json "source": { "type": "vector", "url": "https://free.tilehosting.com/data/v3.json?key=YOUR_KEY" } ``` 4. **Update `sprite` and `glyphs` URLs** *Mapbox defaults*: ```json "sprite": "mapbox://sprites/your-account/streets-v12", "glyphs": "mapbox://fonts/mapbox/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf" ``` → Replace with publicly hosted equivalents, e.g.: ```json "sprite": "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/sprites/liberty", "glyphs": "https://tiles.openfreemap.org/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf" ``` (or use the OpenMapTiles glyph service: `https://free.tilehosting.com/fonts/{fontstack}/{range}.pbf?key=YOUR_KEY`). 5. **Validate the style** ```bash npx gl-style-validate my-style.json ``` Fix any errors reported (missing `source-layer` names, unknown properties, etc.). 6. **Host the JSON** (GitHub Pages, Netlify, your own static server) and point `style:` to that URL. > **Why this works:** MapLibre reads the style JSON exactly like Mapbox GL JS did, but it never contacts `mapbox://` URLs. As long as every external reference (tiles, sprites, glyphs) is reachable **without a token**, the map renders. --- ## 6️⃣ Common pitfalls & how to diagnose them | Symptom | Likely cause | Quick check | |---------|--------------|-------------| | **Blank map, console shows `mapbox://`** | Some source, sprite, or glyph URL still uses the `mapbox://` protocol. | Search your whole project (`Ctrl+Shift+F`) for `mapbox://`. | | **Tiles load but no labels/icons** | Sprite or glyph URLs still point to Mapbox, or `source-layer` names don’t match the new tileset. | Open the style JSON in the browser → verify `sprite` and `glyphs` URLs. Use Maputnik’s “Layers” panel to see the `source-layer` names of the new vector source. | | **CORS error** | The new tile service doesn’t send `Access-Control-Allow-Origin:*`. | Open the tile URL directly in a new tab → see if the browser blocks it. Choose a service that explicitly allows CORS (OpenFreeMap, MapTiler, OpenMapTiles). | | **`401` / `403`** | A hidden Mapbox token is still being sent (e.g., in a plugin). | Disable plugins temporarily; re-enable one-by-one. | | **`map.setFog is not a function`** | You’re still calling a Mapbox-v2-only API. | Replace with `map.setSky(...)` (see the migration guide). | --- ## 7️⃣ TL;DR – One-line “test” solution ```js style: 'https://demotiles.maplibre.org/style.json' // works out-of-the-box, no token ``` If that renders, you know the **MapLibre library itself** is fine. From there you can swap in any of the other URLs above, or start customizing your own style. --- ### 🎯 Next steps after you have a working map 1. **Pick a production-grade tile source** (e.g., self-hosted OpenMapTiles, MapTiler Cloud, or a commercial provider). 2. **Create / edit a style** that references that source (Maputnik is the easiest UI). 3. **Replace any Mapbox-only plugins** (geocoder, directions, draw) with their MapLibre equivalents (see the migration guide). 4. **Test on all target browsers** (MapLibre v5+ now requires WebGL 2). If you run into a specific error while swapping a source or editing a style, drop the exact console message here and I can walk you through that particular fix. Happy mapping!

Description: anti-pattern — assuming Mapbox v2 features work in MapLibre
prompt: I was using Mapbox GL JS v2 in my app, including map.setFog() and some v2-specific camera features. After migrating to MapLibre, these are broken. Did I do something wrong in the migration?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
You haven’t “done anything wrong” – you’ve simply run into the two **Mapbox-v2-only APIs** that MapLibre never implemented. MapLibre forked from Mapbox GL JS v1.13, so anything that first appeared in the Mapbox v2 release (e.g. `setFog`, the free-camera API, `map.getFreeCameraOptions()`, `map.setFreeCameraOptions()`, etc.) does **not exist** in any MapLibre version. Below is a concise checklist that covers the whole migration and then shows the exact replacements for the fog and camera features you’re missing. --- ## 1️⃣ Quick migration sanity-check | ✅ Step | What to verify | Typical symptom if missed | |--------|----------------|---------------------------| | **Package & import** | `npm uninstall mapbox-gl && npm install maplibre-gl`
Import `* as maplibregl` (or `{Map}`) and load `maplibre-gl.css`. | “mapboxgl is not defined” or missing CSS styles. | | **Namespace** | All `mapboxgl` → `maplibregl` (including CSS class prefixes `mapboxgl-` → `maplibregl-`). | Controls or custom UI still use `mapboxgl-ctrl`. | | **Access token** | Remove any `mapboxgl.accessToken = …`. | 401/403 errors from `mapbox://` URLs. | | **Style URL** | Use a non-Mapbox style (e.g. `https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty` or your own exported style). | Blank map or “mapbox://” errors in console. | | **Callbacks → Promises** | Methods like `loadImage`, `GeoJSONSource.getCluster*`, `setRTLTextPlugin` now return a promise. | “callback is not a function” errors. | | **v2-only APIs** | Replace `setFog`, free-camera, and any other v2 methods (see §2). | `map.setFog is not a function`. | | **Plugins** | Swap Mapbox-only plugins for their MapLibre equivalents (`@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder`, `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-draw`, `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-compare`, etc.) or verify they work unchanged. | Missing UI, 401 errors, or console warnings about `mapboxgl` classes. | | **Behaviour changes** | Check for v5/v6 breaking changes (e.g. `map.on` no longer chainable, `canvasContextAttributes` nesting, `styleimagemissing` handling). | Silent failures or unexpected rendering. | If you’ve already cleared steps 1-5 and the only thing still broken is fog / camera, you’re ready for the **API replacements** below. --- ## 2️⃣ Replacing the two v2-only features ### 2.1 Fog → Sky | Mapbox v2 | MapLibre equivalent | How to use it | |-----------|--------------------|---------------| | `map.setFog({ … })` (and `fog` root-level style property) | **`map.setSky({ … })`** (and `sky` root-level style property) | The sky API was added in MapLibre v4.5.0. It provides an atmospheric effect similar to fog, but the property names are different and the visual result is tuned via a *sky* layer rather than a *fog* layer. | #### Example conversion ```js // Mapbox GL JS v2 map.setFog({ "range": [0, 5], "color": "#f8f8f8", "horizon-blend": 0.3 }); ``` ```js // MapLibre GL JS (v4.5+) map.setSky({ // sky-color is the “day” colour; fog-color is the colour of the horizon fog. "sky-color": "#f8f8f8", "horizon-color": "#f8f8f8", "fog-color": "#f8f8f8", // Blend factors – tweak to get the look you want "sky-horizon-blend": 0.3, "fog-ground-blend": 0.5, "atmosphere-blend": 1.0 }); ``` **Style side** – add a top-level `sky` object to your style JSON (or edit it in Maputnik). A minimal sky entry looks like: ```json { "version": 8, "sky": { "type": "sky", "sky-type": "atmosphere", "sky-color": "#199EF3", "horizon-color": "#ffffff", "fog-color": "#c0d8ff", "sky-horizon-blend": 0.5, "fog-ground-blend": 0.5, "atmosphere-blend": 1.0 }, … } ``` > **Tip:** If you only need a simple “fog-like” overlay, you can also add a semi-transparent raster layer on top of the map, but `setSky` is the native replacement. --- ### 2.2 Free-camera API → Camera-options helpers | Mapbox v2 | MapLibre equivalent | |-----------|--------------------| | `map.getFreeCameraOptions()` / `map.setFreeCameraOptions()` (class `FreeCameraOptions`) | **No direct class**. Use the helper `map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation(...)` (v5.0+) or `map.calculateCameraOptionsFromTo(...)` (v2.4+) to produce a regular `CameraOptions` object, then feed it to `jumpTo`, `easeTo`, or `flyTo`. | #### How it works 1. **Calculate the camera options** from the desired lng/lat/alt/rotation. 2. **Apply them** with any of the standard camera movement methods. ```js // Mapbox GL JS v2 – example const freeCam = map.getFreeCameraOptions(); // {center, zoom, pitch, bearing, altitude, roll} map.setFreeCameraOptions({ ...freeCam, altitude: 2000, pitch: 60 }); ``` ```js // MapLibre GL JS (v5+) const camLngLat = [ -122.42, 37.78 ]; // lng, lat const camAlt = 2000; // metres above ground const bearing = 0; // degrees const pitch = 60; // degrees const roll = 0; // degrees (v5+) // 1️⃣ Compute the full CameraOptions object const camOpts = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromCameraLngLatAltRotation( camLngLat, camAlt, bearing, pitch, roll ); // 2️⃣ Move the camera – choose the animation you like map.easeTo(camOpts); // smooth animated move // or map.jumpTo(camOpts); // instant // or map.flyTo(camOpts); // “fly” animation ``` **Older MapLibre (v2-v4)** – the helper `calculateCameraOptionsFromTo` is available: ```js // From point A (camera position) to point B (target) const from = { lngLat: [-122.42, 37.78], altitude: 2000 }; const to = { lngLat: [-122.45, 37.80] }; const camOpts = map.calculateCameraOptionsFromTo(from, to); map.easeTo(camOpts); ``` > **Why the extra step?** MapLibre’s camera model is the same as Mapbox v1 (center-based). The free-camera helpers simply convert a *camera-space* description (lng/lat/alt/rotation) into the *center-based* `CameraOptions` that MapLibre understands. --- ## 3️⃣ What to do next 1. **Add the sky** (or a custom fog layer) to your style and call `map.setSky` once the map is loaded. 2. **Replace any free-camera code** with the `calculateCameraOptions…` → `jumpTo/easeTo/flyTo` pattern shown above. 3. Run your app and open the browser console: * Look for any remaining `mapbox://` URLs (style, source, sprite, glyphs). * Look for `map.setFog` or `map.getFreeCameraOptions` calls that you may have missed. 4. If you still see errors, go back through the **quick-check table** (step 1) and verify each item. 5. Finally, test the map on a **real device** (or at least a browser with WebGL 2) because MapLibre v3+ requires WebGL 2. --- ## 4️⃣ Common follow-up questions | Question | Short answer | |----------|--------------| | *Do I need to keep the Mapbox token for the style?* | No. MapLibre never uses `mapboxgl.accessToken`. All token-related errors mean you still have a `mapbox://` URL somewhere. | | *Can I keep using my Mapbox Studio style?* | Only if you **export the JSON**, replace every `mapbox://` source URL with a non-Mapbox tile source (e.g. an OSM vector tile service), and adjust `source-layer` names to match the new source. | | *What about the `mapbox-gl-draw` plugin?* | It works after a tiny CSS tweak (`.mapboxgl-draw-…` → `.maplibregl-draw-…`). See the MapLibre example “Draw a polygon with mapbox-gl-draw”. If you prefer a native fork, try **Terra Draw**. | | *My map still shows a blank background after the style change.* | Check the **source-layer** names in the style against the tile source you’re using (see the `maplibre-source-wiring` skill). Also verify that the `sprite` and `glyphs` URLs are reachable and not `mapbox://`. | | *Do I need to change the way I load custom images?* | No, `map.loadImage` still works, but remember it now returns a promise: `const {data} = await map.loadImage(url)`. | --- ## 5️⃣ TL;DR – Minimal code snippet ```html
``` Replace the style URL with whatever vector-tile service you plan to use in production, and you’re good

Description: implicit — replacing specific Mapbox plugins after migration
prompt: I'm migrating from Mapbox GL JS to MapLibre. My app uses @mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw for drawing shapes and @mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder for the search box. What do I need to do about each of them?

Description: implicit — unknown plugin status after migration
prompt: I use several Mapbox GL JS plugins in my app and I'm migrating to MapLibre. How do I know which ones will still work?
[groq-gpt-oss] evals/prompts/lib/skill-p:
Below is a quick-reference checklist you can run through for **every Mapbox GL JS plugin** you currently use.  
It tells you how to decide whether the plugin will keep working after you swap to **MapLibre GL JS**, and what to do when it doesn’t.

---

## 1️⃣  Decision matrix – what to look for

| # | Question | What to do if the answer is **yes** | What to do if the answer is **no** |
|---|----------|--------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| 1️⃣ | **Does the plugin call any Mapbox-hosted REST API (Geocoding, Directions, Tiles, Static Images, etc.)?** | You must replace the service (e.g. Nominatim for geocoding, OSRM/ORS for routing, a public vector tile source for tiles) and usually swap the plugin for a MapLibre-compatible fork. | No service call → continue to next check. |
| 2️⃣ | **Does the plugin import `mapbox-gl` (or reference the global `mapboxgl` variable) directly?** | Fork the plugin or use a community-maintained MapLibre version (many popular plugins already have `@maplibre/*` packages). | If it only uses the generic MapLibre API (`map.addSource`, `map.addControl`, etc.) you can keep it unchanged – just change the import/namespace. |
| 3️⃣ | **Does the plugin’s CSS use the `mapboxgl-` class prefix?** | Rename the CSS selectors to `maplibregl-` (or load the plugin’s MapLibre-specific CSS if it ships one). | If the plugin ships a separate stylesheet for MapLibre, swap to that. |
| 4️⃣ | **Does the plugin rely on a Mapbox-only API that MapLibre does not implement?** (e.g. `setFog`, `getFreeCameraOptions`, `setFreeCameraOptions`, `setTerrain` with Mapbox-specific source URLs) | Replace the call with the MapLibre equivalent (`setSky`, `calculateCameraOptions…`, `setTerrain` with a non-Mapbox source) **or** drop the feature. | Refactor the code that uses the missing API; the rest of the plugin may still work. |
| 5️⃣ | **Is the plugin version older than the MapLibre “1.x compatibility branch” (MapLibre v1.x)?** | If you are staying on the compatibility branch (`npm i maplibre-gl@1`), the plugin will likely keep working unchanged. | Upgrade to the latest MapLibre (v6+) and test – you may need a newer fork. |

If you answer **yes** to any of the first three rows, you’ll need to either (a) find a MapLibre-specific fork, or (b) fork/patch the plugin yourself. If you answer **no** to all three, the plugin should work out-of-the-box after you change the import/namespace.

---

## 2️⃣  Common Mapbox plugins – status with MapLibre

| Plugin (npm name) | Works unchanged? | Needs a MapLibre fork / replacement? | What to replace it with (if any) |
|-------------------|------------------|--------------------------------------|----------------------------------|
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw` | **Works** after a tiny CSS tweak (see note) | No, but you must change the CSS class prefix (`.mapboxgl-ctrl-draw*` → `.maplibregl-ctrl-draw*`). | Alternative: **Terra Draw** (`@maplibre/terra-draw`) – actively maintained. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-geocoder` | **Works** with CSS rename and a non-Mapbox geocoder endpoint. | No core change, but you need to point it at a different service (Nominatim, Photon, MapTiler Geocoding, etc.). | **MapLibre-GL-Geocoder** – `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-geocoder`. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-directions` | **Works** only if you replace the backend. | Yes – the plugin expects the Mapbox Directions API. | **MapLibre-GL-Directions** – `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-directions` (works with any OSRM-compatible service). |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-compare` | **Works** after CSS rename (`.mapboxgl-compare*` → `.maplibregl-compare*`). | No, but a MapLibre fork exists. | **MapLibre-GL-Compare** – `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-compare`. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-traffic` | **Does NOT work** – it pulls traffic tiles from Mapbox’s proprietary source. | Yes – you need a different traffic tile provider (e.g. OpenTraffic, TomTom, or a self-hosted vector tile set). | No official MapLibre fork; you’ll need a custom source + style. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-heatmap` (simple heat-map layer helper) | **Works** – it only adds a source/layer using the generic API. | No. | Keep as-is (just change import). |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-inspect` | **Works** after CSS rename. | No. | Keep as-is. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-language` | **Works** – it only swaps label text via the style spec. | No. | Keep as-is. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-legend` | **Works** after CSS rename. | No. | Keep as-is. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-animate-pitch-roll` (custom animation helper) | **Works** if it only uses `map.easeTo`/`flyTo`. | No. | Keep as-is. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-extent` | **Works** – generic API. | No. | Keep as-is. |
| `@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw-polygon` (any other draw-related plugin) | **Check** – most rely on `mapbox-gl-draw` internals, so they inherit the same CSS rename requirement. | Usually works after the base draw plugin is fixed. | Keep as-is. |

> **Tip:** If a plugin’s README mentions “Mapbox GL JS ≥ v2” or “requires a Mapbox access token”, treat it as **needs replacement**.

---

## 3️⃣  How to test each plugin quickly

1. **Swap the import**  
   ```js
   // before
   import MapboxDraw from '@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw';
   // after
   import MapboxDraw from '@mapbox/mapbox-gl-draw';   // same import, but later you’ll change the namespace
   ```
2. **Change the namespace** – wherever you create the map or pass it to the plugin, use `maplibregl` instead of `mapboxgl`.  
   ```js
   const map = new maplibregl.Map({ … });
   const draw = new MapboxDraw({ /* options */ });
   map.addControl(draw);
   ```
3. **Patch CSS** – copy the plugin’s CSS file into your project (or import it) and run a global replace:  
   `mapboxgl-` → `maplibregl-`.  
   If the plugin ships a MapLibre-specific CSS file (e.g. `@maplibre/maplibre-gl-draw/dist/maplibre-gl-draw.css`), import that instead.
4. **Run the app** and open the browser console:  
   * Look for `Uncaught ReferenceError: mapboxgl is not defined` → you missed a namespace reference.  
   * Look for `401`/`403` → a Mapbox service is still being called.  
   * Look for `map.setFog is not a function` → the plugin is using a v2-only API; replace it (see table above).  
5. **Verify UI** – make sure the control button appears, the interaction works, and any network requests go to the new service (e.g. Nominatim instead of `api.mapbox.com`).

If a plugin fails at step 4, consult the **“needs replacement?”** column in the table above. Most of the popular plugins already have a MapLibre-maintained fork; you can find them on npm under the `@maplibre/` scope or by searching “maplibre-gl-*”.

---

## 4️⃣  What to do when a plugin has **no** MapLibre equivalent

1. **Check the source** – many plugins are tiny wrappers around the generic MapLibre API. Fork the repo, replace the single line that imports `mapbox-gl`, change the namespace, and publish a private npm package (or use `patch-package` to apply the change locally).  
2. **Look for an alternative** – the community list **awesome-maplibre** (https://github.com/maplibre/awesome-maplibre) groups plugins by category (UI, Geocoding, Routing, etc.). Search there for a drop-in replacement.  
3. **Implement the missing feature yourself** – because MapLibre’s API is almost identical to Mapbox GL JS v1, you can often copy the plugin’s logic and just swap the namespace. For example, a traffic-layer plugin is just a vector source + style; you can create that yourself with a public traffic tile set.

The old keys are ignored, so a map that relied on them will fall back to the defaults (- `preserveDrawingBuffer: false`, `antialias: true`). **How to fix it** ```js // BEFORE (Mapbox GL JS v2) const map = new mapboxgl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', center: [-122.42, 37.78], zoom: 12, preserveDrawingBuffer: true, antialias: true }); ``` ```js // AFTER (latest maplibre-gl) import * as maplibregl from 'maplibre-gl'; const map = new maplibregl.Map({ container: 'map', style: 'https://tiles.openfreemap.org/styles/liberty', center: [-122.42, 37.78], zoom: 12, // NEW place for the canvas flags canvasContextAttributes: { preserveDrawingBuffer: true, // keep the canvas contents after a render antialias: true // (true is the default, you can omit it) } }); ``` > **Tip:** If you only need `preserveDrawingBuffer` for a one-off screenshot, you can also call `map.getCanvas().toDataURL()` after the map has rendered; the flag is still the most reliable way to guarantee the canvas isn’t cleared. --- ## 2️⃣ Chaining `map.on()` – why it no longer works **What changed?** In MapLibre GL v5 the `Map#on` method stopped returning the map instance. It now returns a **subscription object** (the same object you would later pass to `off`). Because of that, the classic “fluent” style: ```js map.on('load', a).on('click', b); ``` breaks – the second `.on` is called on the subscription, not on the map, and you’ll get a runtime error like *“subscription.on is not a function”*. **Fix options** 1. **Separate calls** – the simplest and most future-proof: ```js map.on('load', a); map.on('click', b); ``` 2. **If you really like chaining**, keep a reference to the map: ```js const m = map .on('load', a); // returns a subscription, but we ignore it m.on('click', b); // `m` is still the original map object ``` (Just don’t try to chain more than one call in a single expression.) 3. **Use the subscription object** – only needed if you plan to later `off` the listener: ```js const loadSub = map.on('load', a); const clickSub = map.on('click', b); // later … loadSub.off(); clickSub.off(); ``` --- ## Quick “Did-you-miss-anything?” Checklist | Item | What to verify / change | |------|--------------------------| | **Package & import** | `npm uninstall mapbox-gl && npm install maplibre-gl`
